question: What does 'patient autonomy' mean in reproductive healthcare?

options.A: The requirement that family elders approve all medical procedures
options.B: The right of the individual to make self-determining choices about their body
options.C: The legal authority of the healthcare provider to choose the best treatment
options.D: The financial independence of the hospital from government oversight

explanation: Autonomy simply means it is the patient's body and their choice. Every individual has the right to decide what happens to their own medical care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is an important nursing check before preparing an infant for a scheduled circumcision?

options.A: Starting an intravenous line in the foot
options.B: Checking when the baby last fed
options.C: Shaving the entire pubic and scrotal hair
options.D: Administering a full dose of oral antibiotics

explanation: Checking the last feeding time helps prevent the baby from vomiting and potentially choking (aspirating) while being handled during the procedure. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h4)

question: How does community stigma usually affect a survivor of gender-based violence?

options.A: It immediately cures all physical infections without needing medicine
options.B: It forces humanitarian agencies to close down local counseling centers
options.C: It drives the survivor into isolation and prevents them from seeking help
options.D: It guarantees that the perpetrator will be publicly arrested by police

explanation: Fear of being judged or blamed makes survivors hide their pain and stay away from the clinics and help they desperately need. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T11#GNS312_U4_T11_h4)

question: Which part of the brain is the main bridge between the nervous and endocrine systems?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Thalamus
options.C: Medulla oblongata
options.D: Cerebellum

explanation: That's correct! The hypothalamus acts as the chief coordinator, linking brain signals to hormone control. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T1#GNS211_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is usually the main problem with lecturing teenagers about making poor food choices?

options.A: It makes them feel judged and causes them to withdraw from counseling.
options.B: Lectures cause an immediate drop in their blood glucose levels.
options.C: It legally violates their medical privacy rights.
options.D: Teens lack the brain development required to understand nutrition.

explanation: Spot on! Teens hate feeling judged. A friendly, supportive chat builds way more trust than an old-school lecture. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h8)

question: Which mental health challenge is commonly seen in teenage mothers after childbirth?

options.A: Postpartum depression
options.B: Schizophrenic psychosis
options.C: Bipolar manic disorder
options.D: Obsessive-compulsive hoarding

explanation: The sudden shift to parenting, lack of emotional maturity, and feeling alone place teenage mothers at high risk for postpartum depression. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h5)

question: Why do whole fruits cause a slower, safer rise in blood sugar than fruit juices?

options.A: Whole fruits contain zero natural sugars unlike juice
options.B: The intact fiber slows down digestion and sugar absorption
options.C: Teexh enzymes block sugar from entering the bloodstream
options.D: Stomach acid instantly destroys all fruit sugars

explanation: Correct! The natural fiber in whole fruits acts like a speed bump, helping your body absorb the sugar nice and slowly. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h4)

question: What normally kicks off a 'secondary' wave of movement (peristalsis) in the oesophagus?

options.A: Distension of the oesophageal wall by a trapped food bolus
options.B: Relaxation of the lower sphincter caused by stomach acid
options.C: Sympathetic stimulation from the thoracic chain ganglia
options.D: Direct voluntary signals sent from the cerebral cortex

explanation: Spot on! If a piece of food gets stuck or stretches the wall, local nerves trigger a secondary squeeze to clear out whatever the first wave left behind. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h4)

question: How does organizing the partograph into specific sections help you as a busy nurse?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need to ever take manual blood pressure
options.B: It reduces the total duration of the first stage of labour by half
options.C: It ensures systematic and organized data collection without missing vital signs
options.D: It allows family members to fill out the medical chart independently

explanation: Having dedicated sections keeps your charting neat and ensures you never forget a vital check for either the mother or her baby. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h2)

question: Why is it important to have family caregivers demonstrate tube care before hospital discharge?

options.A: To legally transfer full liability for the medical device to the family
options.B: To confirm they can safely perform procedures and handle problems at home
options.C: To prove they do not need any further help from home health nurses
options.D: To test whether they can afford expensive commercial feeding pumps

explanation: Return demonstrations ensure that family members have practical competence and confidence to manage tube feedings safely without professional supervision. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h8)

question: Which nursing action shows an unconscious bias against an older patient?

options.A: Speaking slowly and using baby talk when explaining a medication
options.B: Providing written discharge instructions in large print
options.C: Reviewing the medical history with the patient's adult child present
options.D: Asking the patient about their preferred food choices for lunch

explanation: Using baby talk assumes older adults can't understand normal speech. We always want to treat our patients with full dignity! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T10#GNS324_U3_T10_h1)

question: What makes an ectopic pregnancy a major concern for a woman who has had a tubal ligation?

options.A: Sperm can easily bypass the surgical blockages and dissolve the uterine lining.
options.B: If pregnancy occurs, the blocked tube increases the chance the egg implants outside the uterus.
options.C: Hormonal imbalances caused by the surgery force eggs to grow in the abdominal wall.
options.D: The scar tissue prevents the ovaries from releasing any hormones at all.

explanation: While overall pregnancy rates after tubal ligation are very low, any pregnancy that does happen carries a much higher risk of being ectopic, which is a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h6)

question: At what exact times do we check a newborn's Apgar score?

options.A: At birth and every hour for four hours
options.B: At 5 and 10 minutes after birth
options.C: Immediately upon crowning and at delivery
options.D: At 1 and 5 minutes after birth

explanation: We check at 1 minute to see how the baby tolerated birth, and again at 5 minutes to see how they're adjusting to the outside world. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T002#GNS226_U3_T002_h8)

question: A school has broken sewage pipes near the cafeteria and many students are presenting with diarrhea. Which component of the health programme has failed?

options.A: Health education and instruction
options.B: Staff health and welfare
options.C: School health environment
options.D: Physical education and recreation

explanation: Broken sewage and contaminated surroundings represent a breakdown in the physical and sanitary school environment. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of using a Food Frequency Questionnaire?

options.A: It captures long-term dietary patterns and habits
options.B: It prevents patients from ever forgetting yesterday's lunch
options.C: It requires zero participation from the patient
options.D: It provides exact gram weights for every single meal

explanation: You got it! FFQs give you a broad look at a patient's eating habits over weeks or months, rather than just focusing on yesterday's meals. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h3)

question: A 24-year-old woman who used to have regular monthly periods suddenly stops menstruating for eight months. What is this called?

options.A: Primary amenorrhoea
options.B: Secondary amenorrhoea
options.C: Delayed puberty
options.D: Normal variant

explanation: Since she already had established periods before and missed them for over six months, this is classified as secondary amenorrhoea. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why do midwives test pregnant women's urine with a dipstick for protein at every antenatal visit?

options.A: To help screen for early signs of preeclampsia
options.B: To measure the exact glomerular filtration rate
options.C: To check if the mother is drinking enough water
options.D: To confirm the presence of a normal twin pregnancy

explanation: Protein in the urine combined with high blood pressure is an early warning sign of preeclampsia. Routine dipsticks are a simple, life-saving tool in antenatal care! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h6)

question: Which sign strongly points to severe pre-eclampsia in a pregnant mum?

options.A: Painful urination and cloudy urine output
options.B: Itchy skin on the palms and soles of the feet
options.C: Frequent hunger and increased thirst
options.D: Sudden severe headache and high blood pressure

explanation: High BP combined with a terrible headache or vision changes is a classic red flag for severe pre-eclampsia. Keep your eyes peeled for this! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h2)

question: A resident says they feel unsteady walking to the dining hall. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Assess their footwear, use of assistive devices, and recent medications
options.B: Scold the resident for walking without supervision
options.C: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent bathroom trips
options.D: Advise the resident to stay permanently in bed for safety

explanation: Finding the exact cause—like bad shoes, a missing walking stick, or a dizzying drug side effect—helps fix the problem at the root. Spot on! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T13#GNS324_U5_T13_h4)

question: What is the main job of the ascending nerve tracts passing through the brain stem?

options.A: Coordinating balance with the cerebellum
options.B: Carrying sensory signals up to the brain
options.C: Producing automatic breathing rhythms
options.D: Transmitting motor orders down to muscles

explanation: Remember that 'ascending' means going up! These tracts carry sensory information from your body all the way up to higher brain areas. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h3)

question: A nurse notices feelings of personal discomfort when caring for a transgender patient. What is the most professional initial step to take?

options.A: Gently advise the patient to alter their outward gender expression
options.B: Ask another nurse to take over the assignment without explanation
options.C: Reflect on personal biases to ensure they do not affect the quality of care
options.D: Ignore the discomfort and assume it will go away on its own

explanation: Self-reflection is vital for nurses to manage personal attitudes so they can deliver objective, compassionate care to every patient regardless of background. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of segregating medical waste at the point of generation?

options.A: To break the chain of infection
options.B: To speed up trash collection times
options.C: To make hospital cleaning look neat
options.D: To reduce the cost of buying bags

explanation: Separating contaminated waste immediately stops germs from spreading to staff, patients, and the community. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h1)

question: Which of these does NOT cause a mother's heart rate and blood pressure to go up during active labour?

options.A: Complete bed rest and deep sleep
options.B: Physical exertion from pushing
options.C: Uterine contractions
options.D: Labour pain and anxiety

explanation: Exactly right! Labour is intense and exhausting—not a time for quiet sleep and bed rest. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T2#GNS121_U7_T2_h6)

question: Which type of seizure starts in only one specific area of the brain?

options.A: Focal seizure
options.B: Generalized seizure
options.C: Tonic-clonic seizure
options.D: Absence seizure

explanation: Focal seizures originate in a localized region of the brain, affecting only part of the body or awareness. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h3)

question: Why do many young women and teenagers in Nigeria end up turning to unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Preference for traditional herbal remedies over modern medicine
options.B: Easy availability of safe surgical clinics in rural areas
options.C: Lack of financial resources and reproductive health access
options.D: Strict enforcement of mandatory hospital reporting laws

explanation: Poverty, fear of social stigma, and struggling to find safe, legal services often push vulnerable girls into dangerous alternatives. As nurses, keeping our clinics open and welcoming is key to changing this. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h1)

question: A patient with long-term severe bronchitis has a higher risk for which type of urine leakage?

options.A: Overflow incontinence due to a blocked prostate
options.B: Stress incontinence due to repeated pressure from coughing
options.C: Urge incontinence due to bladder muscle irritation
options.D: Functional incontinence due to immobility

explanation: Constant coughing creates repeated downward pressure on the pelvic floor, which can wear down its support over time. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h4)

question: What visual sign inside the catheter hub confirms that the needle has successfully entered the vein?

options.A: A sudden drop in local skin temperature
options.B: Clear fluid filling the plastic chamber
options.C: Air bubbles moving up the tubing
options.D: A flashback of dark red blood

explanation: Blood entering the back of the needle hub proves the tip is sitting inside the blood vessel lumen. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h5)

question: When the kidneys secrete hydrogen ions into the urine, what vital body balance are they maintaining?

options.A: Red blood cell production
options.B: Calcium and bone density
options.C: Acid-base balance
options.D: Blood glucose balance

explanation: Correct! Getting rid of excess hydrogen ions helps clear out acid, keeping your blood pH nicely balanced and steady. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T6#GNS121_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which group of patients has the highest risk of getting burned or injured by hot and cold packs?

options.A: Patients with decreased sensory perception
options.B: Young adults with minor sports bruises
options.C: Patients who are fully alert and active
options.D: Athletes with normal muscle tone

explanation: Always be extra careful with patients who can't feel hot or cold properly—they won't be able to warn you if the pack is hurting their skin! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T8#GNS221_U3_T8_h5)

question: At what centimeter of cervical dilation does the alert line on the partograph traditionally start?

options.A: 10 cm
options.B: 7 cm
options.C: 4 cm
options.D: 1 cm

explanation: Active labour officially kicks off at 4 cm dilation, which is right where the alert line begins on your chart. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h6)

question: What is your main job as a clinic nurse when it comes to family planning reporting?

options.A: Purchasing international medical supplies directly
options.B: Manufacturing contraceptive commodities for the district
options.C: Auditing national health ministry budgets annually
options.D: Gathering and recording service data at the clinic level

explanation: You've got this! Nurses right there at the clinic are the vital first link in capturing client visits and service data accurately. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h1)

question: What do we call the mismatch when a baby's head is too big to fit through the mother's pelvis?

options.A: Uterine inertia
options.B: Secondary power failure
options.C: Occipitoposterior arrest
options.D: Cephalopelvic disproportion

explanation: Spot on! Cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD) simply means the baby's head size or the pelvis shape makes a normal vaginal delivery impossible. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h2)

question: Which organ gets overwhelmed and converts surplus dietary sugars into fat?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Kidneys
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Liver

explanation: Your liver handles the heavy lifting when processing dietary sugars. When it gets overloaded, it converts those extra sugars directly into fat molecules. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h2)

question: When checking a home for safety, which of these is a common physical hazard?

options.A: High white blood cell count
options.B: Elevated resting heart rate
options.C: Incorrect medication dosage
options.D: Loose floor rugs

explanation: Watch out for loose rugs! They are physical hazards that easily cause elderly patients to trip and fall at home. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T9#GNS324_U3_T9_h3)

question: Which graph is better than a pie chart for tracking patient recovery over several months?

options.A: A pie chart
options.B: A line graph
options.C: A raw data list
options.D: A frequency table

explanation: You got it! Line graphs are your best friend for showing changes and trends over time. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T8#GNS217_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why must nurses avoid using stigmatizing language when talking about substance use?

options.A: It is forbidden by international trade agreements
options.B: It causes patients to develop sudden physical allergies
options.C: It drives individuals away from seeking medical help
options.D: It increases the market price of local tobacco products

explanation: Spot on! Stigma creates shame and fear, which pushes people struggling with substance use to hide their problems and avoid clinics. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T14#GNS313_U2_T14_h6)

question: How is community health nursing different from working inside a hospital ward?

options.A: It avoids interaction with families and local groups
options.B: It prioritizes population wellness over individual acute care
options.C: It operates strictly inside enclosed clinic wards
options.D: It relies exclusively on advanced surgical interventions

explanation: Great thinking! Hospital nursing is all about getting the patient stable right by the bedside, whereas community nursing focuses on keeping the whole population well and preventing sickness. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T9#GNS225_U1_T9_h1)

question: What is the best choice when transitioning a patient from liquids to solid foods?

options.A: Tough steak with high-fiber beans
options.B: Heavy, spicy fried chicken and chips
options.C: Soft, bland foods like scrambled eggs or oatmeal
options.D: Crunchy raw vegetables and nuts

explanation: Start slow with soft, gentle foods like pap, oatmeal, or scrambled eggs. They are easy to chew and kind to the healing gut! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T001#GNS227_U6_T001_h7)

question: Why is a highly potent drug not automatically better than a less potent one?

options.A: Potency determines how fast the kidneys excrete the medicine
options.B: Potent drugs cannot bind to cellular receptors
options.C: Less potent drugs always have fewer side effects
options.D: Potency only describes dosage size, not therapeutic success

explanation: Don't confuse small doses with better results! A drug needing a tiny dose just means it's potent, but it might work just as well as a larger dose of another drug. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T6#GNS125_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is cor pulmonale?

options.A: Infection of the heart valves resulting from severe pneumonia
options.B: Narrowing of the coronary arteries due to chronic low blood oxygen
options.C: Weakening of the left ventricle caused by systemic high blood pressure
options.D: Right heart failure caused by primary lung or pulmonary vascular disease

explanation: Spot on! Cor pulmonale happens when lung problems create high pressure in the pulmonary vessels, forcing the right side of the heart to struggle and eventually fail. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h6)

question: In Nigeria, which level of government is primarily responsible for running Primary Health Care (PHC) centers?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Defence
options.B: Private pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Local Government Council
options.D: International Health Organizations

explanation: Spot on! Primary Health Care in Nigeria is managed closely at the grassroots level by Local Government Councils. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of putting a cold pack on a fresh musculoskeletal injury?

options.A: Reducing acute inflammation and numbing localized discomfort
options.B: Stretching tight tendons before physical exercise begins
options.C: Permanently dissolving hardened scar tissue around the joint
options.D: Increasing local blood flow to speed up muscle contractions

explanation: You got it! Cold constricts blood vessels, which keeps swelling down and numbs the sharp pain right after an activity. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h5)

question: A nurse drops a sterile instrument pack on the theatre floor before opening it. What is the correct next step?

options.A: Place the pack back on the shelf for the next procedure
options.B: Open the pack and check if the metal inside looks clean
options.C: Return the pack to the TSSU for complete reprocessing
options.D: Wipe the outside wrapper with alcohol and use it anyway

explanation: You've got this! Once a sterile pack hits the floor, its protective barrier is compromised. You can't trust it anymore—send it back for complete re-sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the single leading cause of maternal death worldwide?

options.A: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Malaria
options.D: Eclampsia

explanation: Severe bleeding after childbirth (PPH) is the number one global killer of new mothers. As a nurse, knowing how to spot and manage PPH is a total lifesaver! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h3)

question: Why are imaging studies like an MRI necessary after finding high hormone levels in the blood?

options.A: To replace the need for baseline blood work entirely
options.B: To locate the physical source or tumor causing the problem
options.C: To measure the exact daily urine output of the patient
options.D: To check if the patient has a secondary bacterial infection

explanation: Blood tests prove a hormone is too high, but imaging helps find the exact spot, like a pituitary tumor, driving the overproduction. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary physiological defect in Type 1 diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.B: Peripheral resistance to the action of insulin
options.C: Temporary glucose intolerance during pregnancy
options.D: Excessive production of glucagon by the liver

explanation: Type 1 diabetes occurs when the immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h1)

question: How does a hiatus hernia make acid reflux worse?

options.A: It disrupts the closing ability of the lower sphincter
options.B: It blocks food from entering the small intestine
options.C: It inflames the lining of the large bowel
options.D: It causes the stomach to produce extra acid daily

explanation: When part of the stomach pushes up through the diaphragm, it messes with the natural pressure barrier that normally keeps food and acid safely locked in the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which tissue type burns more calories at rest?

options.A: Bone matrix
options.B: Blood plasma
options.C: Muscle tissue
options.D: Adipose tissue

explanation: Muscle is metabolically active tissue that burns more energy at rest than fat (adipose) tissue. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h5)

question: Which nursing action helps ensure an accurate blood pressure reading during a screening clinic?

options.A: Using a cuff that is much smaller than the patient's arm circumference
options.B: Allowing the patient to chat actively while the cuff inflates
options.C: Taking the measurement immediately after the patient jogs up the stairs
options.D: Ensuring the patient's arm is supported at heart level with feet flat on the floor

explanation: Proper positioning prevents muscle tension and gravitational artifacts that can falsely raise blood pressure readings. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h6)

question: A hospital quality team wants to know the exact percentage of patients discharged in under four days. Which graph helps find this easiest?

options.A: An ogive
options.B: A stem-and-leaf plot
options.C: A scatter plot
options.D: A pie chart

explanation: Spot on! Ogives shine when we need to find running portions and percentages below or above a specific time frame. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T11#GNS217_U4_T11_h6)

question: What is 'horizontal gene transfer' in bacteria?

options.A: Shedding DNA through normal waste elimination
options.B: Sharing resistance traits directly with other microbes
options.C: Absorbing vitamins directly from human blood vessels
options.D: Passing genetic information strictly to offspring cells

explanation: Bacteria are great at sharing! Horizontal gene transfer lets them pass survival tricks to neighboring germs, even across different species. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T18#GNS313_U1_T18_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing to insert an indwelling urinary catheter for a newly admitted patient. Which technique must the nurse use?

options.A: Surgical asepsis
options.B: Standard precautions only
options.C: Vector control methods
options.D: Medical asepsis

explanation: Inserting a tube into a sterile body cavity like the bladder requires strict surgical asepsis to prevent introducing bacteria. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h5)

question: Why are the spaces (sutures) between the baby's skull bones so important during labour?

options.A: They lock the head in a fixed position to stop accidental rotation.
options.B: They supply oxygen directly to the developing foetal brain tissue.
options.C: They prevent any fluid from entering the cranial vault during birth.
options.D: They allow the skull bones to overlap and reduce the head size.

explanation: Those little gaps act like expansion joints! They let the skull bones slide over each other slightly, making the head a bit smaller so it can fit smoothly through the pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h2)

question: What happens to the tiny coronary blood vessels when local waste products like adenosine pile up?

options.A: They constrict to stop bleeding.
options.B: They harden into rigid fibrous tubes.
options.C: They collapse from high pressure.
options.D: They dilate to increase blood flow.

explanation: Well done! Metabolic waste acts like a chemical green light, telling the blood vessels to relax and open wide so more oxygen can reach hardworking tissues. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T10#GNS111_U2_T10_h3)

question: Why do modern nurse leaders typically combine several management theories instead of using just one?

options.A: All management theories teach the exact same identical concepts
options.B: Hospital accreditation bodies force leaders to memorize all theories
options.C: Healthcare environments are complex and require varied strategies
options.D: It is illegal in most countries to practice only one leadership style

explanation: Because healthcare mixes strict safety rules with human emotions and shifting emergencies, leaders must adapt and mix theories. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which type of transmission happens when tiny germ particles float in the air over long distances?

options.A: Airborne transmission
options.B: Droplet transmission
options.C: Vector-borne transmission
options.D: Contact transmission

explanation: Airborne germs are lightweight and travel far on air currents, unlike heavier droplets that fall quickly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T82#GNS214_U1_T82_h5)

question: Who acts as the central link for coordinating care between the patient and various medical specialists?

options.A: The nurse
options.B: The patient's family
options.C: The hospital accountant
options.D: The pharmacist

explanation: As the nurse, you are the heartbeat of the ward! You coordinate the care plan and make sure information flows smoothly between everyone involved. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h6)

question: A new mother bleeds heavily because a small piece of the placenta was left behind in the uterus. Which of the 4 Ts does this fall under?

options.A: Thrombin
options.B: Tone
options.C: Trauma
options.D: Tissue

explanation: When membranes or pieces of the placenta stay behind inside, we group that under 'Tissue'. Making sure the placenta is complete upon delivery prevents this! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a common fetal complication linked to untreated hyperemesis?

options.A: Intestinal growth restriction
options.B: Low birth weight
options.C: Congenital heart murmurs
options.D: Preterm birth

explanation: Heart defects happen during early structural development, whereas hyperemesis baby issues are usually about poor nutrition and low birth weight. You're mastering neonatal risks! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h4)

question: Why do nursing students learn about population birth trends?

options.A: To calculate national financial budgets for the government
options.B: To accurately predict community maternal and child healthcare needs
options.C: To determine international trade policies for medical goods
options.D: To replace the work of civil registrars and census officers

explanation: You got it! Knowing birth rates helps you anticipate how many mothers and babies will need care in your facility. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h1)

question: Which dangerous emergency involves blood getting trapped inside the spleen, causing a sudden drop in blood volume?

options.A: Splenic sequestration crisis
options.B: Aplastic crisis
options.C: Megaloblastic crisis
options.D: Acute chest syndrome

explanation: In splenic sequestration, blood pools massively inside the spleen. This causes the spleen to swell rapidly and puts the patient into shock very quickly. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h4)

question: A 25-year-old patient comes in with weight gain, facial hair growth, and no periods for 8 months. Which condition fits best?

options.A: Hypothalamic amenorrhea
options.B: Premature ovarian insufficiency
options.C: Polycystic ovary syndrome

question: What is the primary definition of gender-based violence?

question: What is the main goal of food fortification programs in public health?

question: Which of the following is a common myth associated with modern contraceptives?

question: A patient worries that a missing fallopian tube means she can never have a family. What is the best initial nursing response?

question: What is the foramen ovale?

question: Oh no—you accidentally experience a needle-stick injury while in a patient's home. What is your very first move?

question: Why is the intravenous route preferred over oral medications during a severe medical emergency?

question: At what age is primary amenorrhoea typically considered if a young girl has normal breast and pubic hair development but no period yet?

question: Leaving a diaphragm in for way too long can put a patient at risk for which rare, serious condition?

question: What factor most heavily influences how well a newborn with a birth defect will recover?

question: What is the primary reason FGM continues to be practiced in many Nigerian communities?

question: What does we mean when we say there is a disease outbreak?

question: As a nurse, what is your very first priority when a patient arrives with post-abortion complications?

question: When planning a new health program in a village, why is it vital for a nurse to involve local leaders?

question: When you get a cut, your body triggers blood clotting where each step activates even more clotting. What kind of loop is this?

question: Why is teaching the family of a neurological patient just as important as teaching the patient?

question: Which segment of the renal tubule comes immediately after Bowman's capsule?

question: Why does controlling rabies require teamwork between human health workers and vets?
