options.C: It allows nurses to identify, test, and isolate exposed individuals early
options.D: It turns healthy carriers into clinical cases

explanation: Contact tracing helps us track down people who might have been exposed, letting us isolate and care for them before the virus spreads further. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h5)

question: A patient tells you they stopped taking their daily allopurinol because their toe stopped hurting. What is your best nursing advice?

options.A: Suggest they double the dose of allopurinol whenever they eat red meat or drink alcohol
options.B: Confirm that they no longer need any medication since the pain has completely gone away
options.C: Explain that the medication must be taken daily to keep uric acid low and prevent future attacks
options.D: Advise them to switch to taking ibuprofen every time they feel a slight twinge in the toe

explanation: You've got it! Allopurinol isn't a painkiller for a single attack—it's a daily maintenance routine. Stopping it lets uric acid climb right back up and brings the pain back. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h7)

question: What is the main difference between a study conclusion and a recommendation?

options.A: Conclusions are optional, while recommendations are mandatory for all papers
options.B: Conclusions use statistics, while recommendations use personal opinions
options.C: Conclusions summarize main findings, while recommendations suggest future actions
options.D: Conclusions appear in the introduction, while recommendations are in the abstract

explanation: A conclusion wraps up what you found out, while a recommendation suggests what should be done next in practice. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h8)

question: What is the main goal of a nursing interview?

options.A: To prescribe appropriate medications
options.B: To diagnose complex psychiatric illnesses
options.C: To gather health data and assess symptoms
options.D: To perform surgical procedures safely

explanation: You've got this! A nursing interview is simply about collecting info on the patient's health and history so you can care for them properly. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why must a nurse understand normal vital sign ranges instead of just memorizing numbers?

options.A: To prescribe corrective medications without a doctor
options.B: To quickly spot abnormal values and report critical changes to the medical team
options.C: To avoid ever taking manual vitals again
options.D: To grade other nursing students on clinical exams

explanation: Spot on! Knowing what's normal helps you catch early signs of trouble so the team can jump in and help the patient fast. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T4#GNS123_U2_T4_h6)

question: A nurse manager finds widespread failure in following a new infection control standard on the ward. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Investigate the root cause to see if supplies or training are lacking
options.B: Remove all handwashing stations from the clinical floor
options.C: Ignore the results because standards are rarely met anyway
options.D: Immediately suspend all nurses working on the morning shift

explanation: Good managers look for systemic reasons behind poor compliance, such as missing supplies or poor training, before blaming staff. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h7)

question: When doing a 24-hour dietary recall, what does the nurse ask the client to do?

options.A: List everything they ate over the past 24 hours
options.B: Predict their exact food budget for the coming year
options.C: Fast for a full day before visiting the clinic
options.D: Cook a demonstration meal for the nursing staff

explanation: Easy peasy! A 24-hour dietary recall is simply asking the client to list everything they ate and drank recently. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T002#GNS227_U3_T002_h2)

question: Why do we encourage mothers to start breastfeeding right after birth?

options.A: It prevents the mother from experiencing postpartum depression
options.B: It ensures the baby sleeps through the entire first night
options.C: It eliminates the need for any future vitamin supplements
options.D: It stimulates uterine contractions and helps milk production

explanation: Nature is amazing! Nursing releases oxytocin, which naturally helps the uterus contract down to reduce bleeding while getting milk flowing for baby. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is the main difference between a regular hospital bed and a smart bed?

options.A: Smart beds require manual hand cranks for all adjustments
options.B: Smart beds are exclusively used in outpatient surgical clinics
options.C: Smart beds integrate computerized systems and sensors for monitoring
options.D: Smart beds cannot be adjusted for patient height or seating angles

explanation: Smart beds are great because they have built-in sensors and computer tech to track patient vitals automatically, unlike old-school manual beds! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why do some heart tumours cause symptoms that look just like regular heart failure?

options.A: The tumour causes the coronary arteries to permanently spasm
options.B: The tumour takes up space in the heart chambers and reduces the amount of blood pumped out
options.C: Cardiac tumours completely stop the production of red blood cells
options.D: Cardiac tumours directly destroy the brain's ability to regulate heart rate

explanation: When an extra mass takes up room inside the heart, the chambers can't hold or push out enough blood. This causes fluid to back up, mimicking heart failure. Great job thinking it through! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T8#GNS213_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why do patients dealing with chronic pain often have terrible sleep problems?

options.A: Physical pain forces the brain to produce excessive amounts of melatonin.
options.B: Analgesic medications always cause permanent destruction of REM sleep cycles.
options.C: Pain triggers physical discomfort that prevents the nervous system from relaxing into sleep.
options.D: Chronic pain completely eliminates the need for stage three sleep.

explanation: Constant physical discomfort acts like a stress alarm, keeping the nervous system fired up and making it really hard to slip into deep, continuous sleep. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h4)

question: Besides eating healthy food, what is the big benefit of practicing portion control?

options.A: Maintaining energy balance and preventing excessive weight gain
options.B: Ensuring that digestion takes place only during nighttime hours
options.C: Eliminating the need to consume any carbohydrates at all
options.D: Reducing the body's overall requirement for clean drinking water

explanation: Exactly. Portion control stops us from taking in more energy than we burn off, helping us stay at a healthy weight. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h5)

question: A community health nurse in rural Nigeria uses a mobile phone app to track children's immunizations. What does this show?

options.A: The integration of technology into modern community health practice
options.B: A complete return to medieval religious care giving methods
options.C: The abandonment of primary healthcare principles
options.D: An illegal practice that violates public health policies

explanation: Just like you using this CBT app on your phone, modern nurses use digital tools every day to make healthcare smarter and faster! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h7)

question: What is the main medical treatment needed for a diagnosed breast abscess?

options.A: Application of warm compresses only
options.B: Immediate and permanent weaning
options.C: Surgical drainage of pus combined with antibiotics
options.D: Strict bed rest without medication

explanation: Antibiotics alone can't clear a walled-off pocket of pus, so the trapped fluid needs to be safely drained. Excellent clinical reasoning! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h6)

question: Why do we carry out a re-audit near the end of a quality improvement cycle?

options.A: To find new reasons to query junior nursing staff members
options.B: To see if the corrective actions successfully improved care
options.C: To comply with international travel laws for nurses
options.D: To increase the amount of paperwork stored in the archive

explanation: Spot on! A re-audit helps us check whether the changes we put in place actually solved the problems we found during our first check. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the main cause of an ischemic stroke?

options.A: Sudden systemic drop in normal body temperature
options.B: Uncontrolled electrical discharge across the motor cortex
options.C: Rupture of a weakened blood vessel inside the brain tissue
options.D: Occlusion of a cerebral artery by a thrombus or embolus

explanation: An ischemic stroke happens when a blood clot blocks a brain vessel, cutting off the oxygen and nutrients that part of the brain needs. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T19#GNS222_U3_T19_h4)

question: What does a drug's half-life represent in pharmacokinetics?

options.A: The time it takes for the body to absorb half of an oral dose
options.B: The time it takes for blood concentration of the drug to decrease by 50 percent
options.C: The exact number of hours a drug remains active in the stomach
options.D: The time required for the liver to metabolize half of the active ingredient

explanation: Half-life measures how long it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to drop down to half of its previous level. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T4#GNS125_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which type of food hazard includes cleaning chemicals and leftover pesticide sprays?

options.A: Physical hazards
options.B: Biological hazards
options.C: Nutritional hazards
options.D: Chemical hazards

explanation: You guessed it—chemical hazards involve toxic substances like cleaning agents and farm chemicals that accidentally get into our food supply. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h1)

question: What is the main danger when a nurse transcribes (copies) a medication order?

options.A: It removes the need for nurses to check patient identity
options.B: It makes doctors write prescriptions much slower than usual
options.C: It permanently deletes previous medication history from the chart
options.D: It introduces opportunities for human error and misinterpretation

explanation: Spot on! Every time an order is manually copied over, there's a risk that numbers, decimals, or abbreviations might be misread. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h6)

question: When is the right time to change an absorbent diaper or pad for your patient?

options.A: Right before the doctor arrives for ward round
options.B: As soon as the patient complains of feeling hungry
options.C: Promptly whenever it becomes soiled or wet
options.D: Only once every twenty-four hours during the morning shift

explanation: Don't wait for a schedule if comfort and skin health are on the line. Check frequently and change diapers right away when they are wet or soiled. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h4)

question: Which type of diarrhoea happens when inflammation causes blood, pus, and mucus to leak into the bowel?

options.A: Osmotic diarrhoea
options.B: Secretory diarrhoea
options.C: Exudative diarrhoea
options.D: Motility diarrhoea

explanation: When the gut lining gets inflamed and 'weeps' fluid, blood, or mucus—like in a bad infection or IBD—we call it exudative diarrhoea. Great nursing vocabulary to keep in your toolkit! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the main job of the anterior pituitary gland in the neuroendocrine system?

options.A: It generates electrical impulses for sympathetic flight responses
options.B: It monitors blood glucose levels via direct humoral sensation
options.C: It releases tropic hormones in response to hypothalamic signals
options.D: It stores oxytocin and antidiuretic hormone produced by neurons

explanation: The anterior pituitary takes messages from the hypothalamus and releases its own hormones to control other glands in the body. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T6#GNS211_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which of the following is a non-modifiable risk factor for cancer?

options.A: Smoking
options.B: Alcohol use
options.C: Diet
options.D: Age

explanation: Age is an inherent biological factor that cannot be altered, making it non-modifiable. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h4)

question: A postpartum mother had a very long labor and an emergency cesarean section. Which condition is she most at risk for developing?

options.A: Cervical polyps
options.B: Endometritis
options.C: Uterine prolapse
options.D: Ovarian cysts

explanation: Long labors and C-sections mean the uterus is exposed for a longer time, which greatly increases the risk of bacteria getting inside and causing endometritis. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h2)

question: Why is retraining better than punishing staff when errors pop up in data collection?

options.A: Staff members prefer being disciplined over learning new skills
options.B: Retraining is always cheaper than buying new paper forms
options.C: Punitive measures violate international supply chain laws
options.D: Punishment encourages staff to hide mistakes rather than fix them

explanation: You got it! When people are terrified of punishment, they fake records to look flawless, which ruins the reliability of our health data. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h7)

question: What does a valid research instrument do?

options.A: Measures what it is supposed to measure
options.B: Costs very little money to print out
options.C: Takes less than five minutes to finish
options.D: Gives the exact same results every time

explanation: Validity is all about accuracy, meaning the tool actually captures the specific concept being studied. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h2)

question: Which nutrient is most often missing in unfortified gluten-free grain alternatives?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Potassium
options.C: B vitamins
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Standard wheat products are usually fortified with B vitamins like folate, which alternative flours often lack unless added back. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of patient safety measures in a hospital?

options.A: To prevent harm and medical errors during care
options.B: To lower the cost of purchasing medical drugs
options.C: To speed up the discharge process for doctors
options.D: To reduce the total number of hospital beds

explanation: Patient safety is centered entirely on stopping avoidable injuries and medical mistakes before they harm the person receiving treatment. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which bone shape category does the patella ( kneecap) belong to?

options.A: Flat bone
options.B: Irregular bone
options.C: Long bone
options.D: Sesamoid bone

explanation: Sesamoid bones like the patella develop inside tendons to protect them from excessive wear and tear. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why is it important for nurses to ask direct questions about hopelessness to clients with chronic illness?

options.A: To uncover hidden thoughts of depression or self-harm early
options.B: To make the client stop talking about their physical pain
options.C: To prove to the doctor that the client has a psychiatric disorder
options.D: To fill out the hospital admission paperwork faster

explanation: Directly asking about emotional pain allows nurses to protect vulnerable clients and provide timely mental health support. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the main job of cortisol during the stress response?

options.A: To lower blood pressure and slow down breathing
options.B: To enhance immune system activity and fight infection
options.C: To raise blood glucose and supply energy to vital organs
options.D: To stimulate digestion and nutrient absorption

explanation: Cortisol acts like an emergency power switch, boosting your blood sugar so your brain and muscles have the immediate fuel they need to react. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T8#GNS123_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why is it so helpful to compare a patient's current weight to their usual baseline weight?

options.A: It proves the weighing scale is working properly
options.B: It helps spot meaningful weight gains or losses over time
options.C: It is the only legal requirement for ward admission charting
options.D: It completely replaces the need for a BMI calculation

explanation: Comparing against the patient's own baseline shows personal health trends that standard population charts might miss. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T004#GNS227_U5_T004_h3)

question: How would you best describe depression in a clinical setting?

options.A: A temporary lack of vitamins causing physical weakness
options.B: A minor behavioral adjustment issue in older adults
options.C: A serious mood disorder affecting thoughts and daily activities
options.D: A temporary emotional reaction to physical fatigue

explanation: Spot on! Depression isn't just a brief bad mood or fatigue; it's a true mood disorder that impacts a person's entire daily life and well-being. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T2#GNS324_U4_T2_h1)

question: A nurse is preparing to give a 10:00 AM medication dose using the unit dispensing cart. When is the best time to document that the drug was given?

options.A: Whenever the nurse remembers during the afternoon visiting hours
options.B: Before leaving the central pharmacy room with the mobile drug cart
options.C: Immediately after the patient swallows the medication at the bedside
options.D: At the end of the shift when all patient charts are gathered together

explanation: Documentation must happen right after administration to prevent accidental double-dosing or missed records. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is a major downside of a healthcare system that focuses only on big hospitals?

options.A: It provides too many vaccines directly inside family homes
options.B: It neglects preventive care and ignores rural or poor communities
options.C: It focuses too much on keeping people healthy
options.D: It relies entirely on community health workers instead of doctors

explanation: Exactly. When everything is locked inside city hospitals, people in remote areas miss out on basic checkups and early care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is a major reason people in Nigeria often delay going to modern hospitals?

options.A: An excess of free hospitals in every rural village
options.B: Mandatory international health insurance for all citizens
options.C: The complete absence of any traditional healing practices
options.D: Financial constraints and out-of-pocket health spending

explanation: True. Having to pay out-of-pocket without easy health insurance often makes folks wait until an illness gets really bad before seeking care. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h7)

question: As a nurse, why should you carefully review published research before using it?

options.A: To decide if findings are safe and appropriate to apply to patients
options.B: To find grammatical errors in academic writing
options.C: To publish their own papers in foreign journals
options.D: To prove that researchers always make mistakes

explanation: You've got this! Checking research helps you figure out what is actually safe and helpful to bring into your daily ward routine. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T2#GNS217_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which rare, serious skin and tissue condition can develop in patients with bad kidney function who receive gadolinium contrast?

options.A: Acute radiation sickness
options.B: Chronic bone marrow failure
options.C: Malignant hyperthermia crisis
options.D: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis

explanation: Well done! Gadolinium can trigger this serious condition in patients whose kidneys are struggling to filter waste. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is a major drawback of relying only on traditional lectures in nursing training?

options.A: It takes too much time to cover basic medical definitions
options.B: It prevents the instructor from using any visual aids like slides
options.C: It can leave students passive and rarely tests their practical clinical skills
options.D: It requires every student to have a private computer in the hall

explanation: Lectures are great for blasting through a lot of theory quickly, but they don't give you much hands-on practice or test your real-time clinical judgment. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h2)

question: What is a major goal of community-based contraceptive distribution programs?

options.A: Eliminating the need for client confidentiality and records
options.B: Removing all nurses from government health clinics permanently
options.C: Increasing the financial profit of local pharmaceutical companies
options.D: Bringing supplies closer to clients in remote rural areas

explanation: Bringing care straight to rural villages ensures that distance doesn't stop anyone from getting the reproductive health supplies they need. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h7)

question: A 30-week pregnant woman comes to the clinic complaining of a severe headache and blurred vision. What is your very first nursing action?

options.A: Discharge her home with instructions to eat more salt
options.B: Assess her blood pressure for signs of dangerous hypertension
options.C: Schedule her for routine tetanus vaccination next month
options.D: Encourage her to walk around the ward to improve circulation

explanation: Well done! Severe headaches and vision changes are classic danger signs of preeclampsia. Checking her blood pressure right away is a life-saving priority. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h2)

question: What does health literacy refer to in nursing practice?

options.A: The number of medical books a patient has read at home
options.B: A person's ability to understand and use basic health information
options.C: How fast a client can write down their doctor's name
options.D: The level of education the nurse completed in school

explanation: Health literacy is the practical skill of understanding medical instructions, prescriptions, and health advice. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which four elements form the main building blocks of most nutrients in our diet?

options.A: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen
options.B: Phosphorus, sulfur, chlorine, and magnesium
options.C: Calcium, iron, sodium, and potassium
options.D: Copper, zinc, iodine, and manganese

explanation: Spot on! These four simple elements form the chemical backbone of the carbohydrates, fats, proteins, and nucleic acids we eat every day. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h1)

question: When should active teenagers drink water during sports or exercise?

options.A: Only when they feel a strong sense of thirst
options.B: Regularly throughout the day and during activity, before feeling thirsty
options.C: Only during meal times with solid food
options.D: Exclusively after finishing all sports or exercises

explanation: Good to know! Thirst usually means the body is already slightly dehydrated, so it's best to sip water steadily before feeling extremely thirsty. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h4)

question: Which finding around a drainage tube insertion site is a sign of a potential infection?

options.A: Clear pink fluid on the outer dressing
options.B: Purulent discharge and foul odor
options.C: A small amount of dried blood at the stitch
options.D: Soft skin that feels cool to the touch

explanation: Pus and bad smells are classic indicators that bacteria are multiplying at the wound site, signaling a developing infection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h2)

question: Which task best shows a staff nurse directly participating in quality assurance?

options.A: Reporting a faulty intravenous pump before it harms a patient
options.B: Complaining about low salary during a shift handover
options.C: Refusing to help clean a patient after an accident
options.D: Leaving ward charts blank until the end of the week

explanation: Brilliant! Spotting a broken tool and speaking up before it hurts a patient is the textbook definition of proactive quality assurance in action. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is a key prevention message nurses should teach families to stop Lassa fever at home?

options.A: Keep doors and windows wide open during the evening hours
options.B: Dry all harvested grains directly on bare soil surfaces
options.C: Store food items in tightly sealed, rodent-proof containers
options.D: Keep pet cats away from all residential cooking areas

explanation: Locking up food in secure containers keeps rats away and stops them from contaminating your grains with urine and faeces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T8#GNS214_U1_T8_h9)

question: Why is keeping our environment clean considered a primary defense against diseases?

options.A: It permanently alters the genetic makeup of pathogens so they become harmless
options.B: It ensures that community members never come into contact with wild animals
options.C: It replaces the need for any form of medical treatment during disease outbreaks
options.D: It removes the breeding grounds and shelter that vectors and pests need to survive

explanation: You got it! A clean environment denies pests the food, water, and shelter they need to multiply. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is an organ made of?

options.A: Individual atoms bonded tightly into complex organic molecules
options.B: A collection of identical cells performing the exact same task
options.C: Two or more different types of tissues working together
options.D: Multiple organ systems functioning inside a single body cavity

explanation: Think of an organ like a team! It takes different tissue types working together—like muscle and lining tissues—to get a big job done. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: How does hiring discrimination typically affect a person with a physical disability?

options.A: It encourages employers to fund public transport
options.B: It eliminates the need for ramps
options.C: It guarantees higher government payouts
options.D: It forces qualified individuals into underemployment or total dependence

explanation: When workplaces shut their doors due to unfair biases, capable people lose their chance to earn an independent living. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T12#GNS225_U5_T12_h4)

question: Which action directly targets a human reservoir to stop an infection from spreading?

options.A: Boiling all municipal drinking water before distribution
options.B: Placing metal wire mesh over livestock feed storage
options.C: Spraying heavy insecticides around outdoor garbage dumps
options.D: Administering curative drug therapy to clear the pathogen

explanation: Giving medications clears the germs right out of the human body, turning off that human reservoir. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h6)

question: Under Nigerian law, when is an abortion legally allowed?

options.A: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.B: When the pregnancy is a result of rape
options.C: When there is severe financial hardship
options.D: Whenever the woman requests it

explanation: Nigerian law permits termination only when it is strictly necessary to save the mother's life. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h8)

question: Because a pregnant teenager's pelvis is still growing, she is at higher risk for which complication?

options.A: Obstructed labor
options.B: Chronic heart failure
options.C: Placental overgrowth
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: You're doing great! An immature pelvis may not be wide enough for the baby to pass through easily, raising the risk of obstructed labor. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the large intestine during digestion?

options.A: Producing digestive enzymes for proteins
options.B: Absorbing water and salts from waste
options.C: Initiating the chemical digestion of food
options.D: Breaking down fats into fatty acids

explanation: The large intestine mainly acts to pull water and essential salts back into the body, turning liquid waste into formed stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h1)

question: When is the best time for a nurse to educate an expectant mum about potential prenatal vitamin side effects?

options.A: At the child's one-year checkup
options.B: Only after a fecal impaction occurs
options.C: Early in the prenatal care schedule
options.D: During the postpartum hospital discharge

explanation: Brilliant! Teaching mums early means they can adjust their diet and water intake before vitamin side effects become a painful problem. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h8)

question: A teenager expresses a belief that getting pregnant or catching an infection is impossible for them. Which psychological concept is this youth displaying?

options.A: Cognitive dissonance
options.B: Depressive withdrawal
options.C: Prefrontal cortex maturity
options.D: Personal invulnerability

explanation: Believing that negative health outcomes only affect other people is a classic sign of the adolescent sense of personal invulnerability. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h3)

question: A nurse is writing an introduction for a study on hand hygiene. What is the main goal of this section?

options.A: Summarizing the final statistical data collected from the hospital wards
options.B: Establishing the gap in current compliance knowledge and stating study aims
options.C: Providing personal opinions on why hospital staff refuse to wash hands
options.D: Listing every historical discovery of microscopic bacteria since the nineteenth century

explanation: The introduction sets the stage by showing what we already know, what is missing, and why this study is so important. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why must nurses watch a mother and newborn extra closely immediately after delivery?

options.A: A high proportion of maternal and newborn deaths happen within the first 48 hours
options.B: The mother is usually discharged home immediately without any risk
options.C: Hormonal changes stop completely after the placenta is delivered
options.D: Newborns do not require feeding assistance until day three of life

explanation: The first 48 hours are the riskiest time for sudden bleeding, infections, or newborn collapse. Close monitoring keeps both mum and baby safe! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h4)

question: Which hormone from the pituitary gland shoots up as the body approaches menopause?

options.A: Adrenocorticotropic hormone
options.B: Human growth hormone
options.C: Thyroid-stimulating hormone
options.D: Follicle-stimulating hormone

explanation: Think of the pituitary gland shouting louder (making more FSH) when the ovaries stop responding. Great revision point! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T15#GNS121_U5_T15_h2)

question: How do major structural uterine defects often lead to repeated miscarriages?

options.A: By permanently destroying all hormones needed to maintain a menstrual cycle
options.B: By limiting the physical space available for normal fetal growth and disrupting proper implantation
options.C: By stopping the ovaries from releasing mature eggs every month
options.D: By completely blocking blood flow to the lower extremities

explanation: That is correct! An irregular or restricted uterine cavity makes it hard for a growing embryo to implant safely and find enough room to develop. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T19#GNS216_U5_T19_h5)

question: A 45-year-old woman comes to the clinic with a hard, painless breast lump she noticed six months ago. What often causes this kind of late presentation in our communities?

options.A: Cultural stigma and trying alternative therapies first
options.B: The lump grew instantly overnight
options.C: Routine mammograms are done everywhere
options.D: The tumor was already surgically removed

explanation: Fear, stigma, and trying traditional remedies first are real barriers our patients face. As nurses, part of our job is compassionate, judgment-free education. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h3)

question: What is a key nursing check before giving medication to a pregnant patient?

options.A: Obtain written consent from the hospital pharmacist
options.B: Perform a complete surgical review of systems
options.C: Verify gestational age and assess fetal heart rate
options.D: Prescribe an alternative drug with fewer side effects

explanation: Always check how far along she is and how the baby is doing first, to make sure the drug is safe for that specific stage of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T5#GNS215_U6_T5_h8)

question: When is using a mucous membrane route (like sublingual or rectal) a lifesaver for a patient?

options.A: When the patient needs a subcutaneous injection
options.B: When the medication must bypass the skin entirely
options.C: When the patient is unable to swallow oral medications
options.D: When the drug requires slow digestion in the stomach

explanation: Spot on! If a patient is too weak, drowsy, or vomiting too much to swallow pills, routes like under the tongue or rectally keep their treatment going smoothly. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T15#GNS125_U3_T15_h1)

question: Which of these is one of Elisabeth Kübler-Ross's classic stages of grief?

options.A: Bargaining
options.B: Isolation
options.C: Revenge
options.D: Forgetfulness

explanation: Spot on! Bargaining is that stage where a person tries to negotiate a different reality. It sits right alongside denial, anger, depression, and acceptance. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T10#GNS321_U4_T10_h2)

question: How does educating girls and women directly improve maternal health in a community?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for hospitals and clinics
options.B: It empowers women to recognize pregnancy danger signs and seek prompt medical care
options.C: It guarantees that every woman will become a qualified midwife
options.D: It prevents women from ever getting pregnant

explanation: Education is powerful! When women understand health risks, they can spot danger early and make smart choices for themselves and their babies. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h3)

question: A client is finding it hard to stick to a new meal plan. What should you do as the nurse?

options.A: Scold the client for lacking discipline and willpower
options.B: Adjust the plan to include small, realistic, and affordable changes
options.C: Insist the client eat only bland hospital-style food
options.D: Discontinue all nutritional counseling immediately

explanation: Wonderful nursing approach! Small, realistic steps help clients build lasting habits without feeling overwhelmed. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T002#GNS227_U3_T002_h4)

question: Which principle ensures that health services are affordable and located where young people can easily reach them?

options.A: Appropriateness
options.B: Accessibility
options.C: Acceptability
options.D: Equity

explanation: Spot on! Accessibility is all about removing financial, physical, and time barriers so young people can actually get to the clinic. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T17#GNS312_U3_T17_h3)

question: Where in the body would you look for multi-unit smooth muscle?

options.A: In the walls of the urinary bladder
options.B: In the iris of the eye controlling the pupil
options.C: In the muscular walls of the stomach
options.D: In the middle layer of the small intestine

explanation: Multi-unit muscle gives us fine, precise control—just like adjusting your camera lens or how your iris changes the pupil size in bright light! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h4)

question: Why might a nurse researcher choose an observation study instead of an experiment for ethical reasons?

options.A: Observational studies cost more money to run
options.B: It is unethical to deliberately expose patients to harm
options.C: Hospital management bans all experimental laboratory work
options.D: Patients prefer answering surveys over taking medications

explanation: You nailed it! Patient safety comes first. If an experiment puts participants at risk, we cannot ethically test it directly on them. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T3#GNS224_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which famous nursing theorist built her work around the patient's ability to perform self-care?

options.A: Callista Roy
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Dorothea Orem
options.D: Madeleine Leininger

explanation: Correct! Dorothea Orem's Self-Care Deficit Theory focuses on stepping in to help patients when they cannot manage their own self-care. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is a key focus during post-test counselling for a client who tests negative?

options.A: Discussing prevention methods and the window period
options.B: Reporting the client to local security agencies
options.C: Isolating the client from their family members
options.D: Starting immediate lifelong antiretroviral treatment

explanation: Negative results require education on staying negative and understanding that recent exposures might not show up immediately during the window period. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of a high calorie diet?

options.A: To lower baseline blood pressure
options.B: To restrict daily sodium intake
options.C: To achieve a positive energy balance
options.D: To speed up digestive transit time

explanation: A high calorie diet is meant to supply more energy than the body burns, creating a positive balance to promote weight gain and healing. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of writing an incident report when a medical error or near-miss happens?

options.A: To find someone to blame and punish immediately
options.B: To increase paperwork for the nursing administration
options.C: To hide the mistake from the hospital management
options.D: To find root causes and prevent future occurrences

explanation: Spot on! Incident reports are learning tools to improve system safety, not weapons to punish individual nurses. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T4#GNS312_U5_T4_h3)

question: How can you overcome the blocking effect of a competitive antagonist?

options.A: By cooling the patient's body temperature
options.B: By increasing the dose of the agonist
options.C: By waiting for the kidneys to shut down
options.D: By administering an entirely unrelated vitamin

explanation: Because they fight for the same spot, you can crowd out the blocker by simply flooding the system with more of the agonist. Brilliant and logical! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T7#GNS125_U5_T7_h2)

question: Why is studying bacterial genetics so important for managing infections in hospitals today?

options.A: It guarantees that bacteria will instantly vanish from hospital environments
options.B: It explains how bacteria share genes and develop resistance to common antibiotics
options.C: It eliminates the need for nurses to practice standard infection control
options.D: It proves that microorganisms can transform spontaneously into human cells

explanation: Knowing bacterial genetics helps us track how superbugs share resistance genes, which is vital for patient safety! [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of the cold chain in immunization programs?

options.A: To speed up the delivery of medical supplies to large cities
options.B: To keep vaccines within safe temperature ranges so they remain potent
options.C: To store expired medications safely away from patients
options.D: To freeze liquid vaccines completely solid before use

explanation: The cold chain protects heat-sensitive vaccines from losing their medical effectiveness before they reach the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h4)

question: Which period is known to be the trickiest for medication errors and missed care?

options.A: Attending a family gathering on the weekend
options.B: Moving between hospitals, rehab facilities, and home
options.C: Routine visits to the local outdoor market
options.D: Switching from daytime clothes to nightwear

explanation: Correct! Whenever a patient moves from one place of care to another, things easily get mixed up or forgotten. That's why we stay extra alert! [learn more](GNS324_U1_T3#GNS324_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is a major risk of maintaining unsafe patient-to-nurse ratios?

options.A: Crucial changes in patient condition can be missed
options.B: Doctors will have to write fewer prescriptions
options.C: Patients will be discharged much earlier than planned
options.D: Hospital electricity bills will automatically increase

explanation: When nurses are overworked with too many patients, subtle signs of deterioration are harder to catch in time. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h5)

question: Which validated tool is commonly used in clinical practice to assess a patient's risk for developing pressure injuries?

options.A: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.B: Braden Scale
options.C: Morse Fall Scale
options.D: APGAR Score

explanation: The Braden Scale evaluates sensory perception, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition, and friction/shear to score a patient's pressure injury risk. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h7)

question: A patient walks into the clinic with lower tummy pain and unusual discharge. What serious upper-body complication should a nurse watch out for if this is left untreated?

options.A: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Chronic hypertension
options.D: Type 2 diabetes mellitus

explanation: If a lower infection is ignored, it can travel upwards into the reproductive organs and trigger pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h3)

question: What is one of the main duties of a community health nurse regarding occupational safety?

options.A: Educating workers on hazard recognition and protective gear
options.B: Designing industrial machinery for manufacturing companies
options.C: Enforcing labor laws through police intervention
options.D: Managing the financial accounts of private factories

explanation: Community nurses shine at health education—teaching everyday workers how to spot dangers and use protective gear correctly. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h7)

question: What is the main goal of using clot-busting (thrombolytic) therapy in an acute ischemic stroke?

options.A: To prevent future heart attacks from occurring
options.B: To dissolve the blood clot and restore blood flow
options.C: To lower systemic blood pressure instantly
options.D: To shrink swollen brain tissue caused by edema

explanation: You got it! Thrombolytic therapy breaks down the clot blocking the vessel, getting oxygen flowing back to starving brain cells quickly. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h6)

question: Standard precautions must be applied to which group of patients?

options.A: Only patients with confirmed blood-borne viruses
options.B: Patients admitted to the surgical ward only
options.C: All patients regardless of their diagnosis
options.D: Individuals showing visible signs of a fever

explanation: Standard precautions assume any patient fluid could carry pathogens, protecting nurses and patients alike during every encounter. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which blood product is usually given to replace multiple missing clotting factors in a patient with severe liver disease?

options.A: Packed red blood cells
options.B: Normal saline solution
options.C: Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP)
options.D: Ringer's lactate solution

explanation: Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) is packed with all the liquid plasma proteins and clotting factors a failing liver can no longer make on its own. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T11#GNS311_U2_T11_h7)

question: How do nursing interventions help restore balance in a sick patient?

options.A: By stopping the patient from eating or drinking
options.B: By supporting or taking over failing regulatory systems
options.C: By replacing all natural body organs with machines
options.D: By curing viral infections without the use of drugs

explanation: Exactly right! As a nurse, you step in to help with breathing, hydration, or circulation whenever the patient's body needs backup. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T7#GNS123_U1_T7_h6)

question: How do the circular folds inside the small intestine help us absorb more nutrients?

options.A: They pump water directly out of the lumen via active transport
options.B: They produce bile salts necessary for the emulsification of dietary fats
options.C: They slow down chyme movement and increase contact with the absorptive surface
options.D: They secrete powerful hydrochloric acid to break down stubborn proteins

explanation: Great job! These folds act like speed bumps in the intestines, making the food mixture spiral around so it spends more time touching the walls for better absorption. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T012#GNS227_U1_T012_h2)

question: Where does the vast majority of tubular reabsorption take place within the nephron?

options.A: Glomerular capsule
options.B: Proximal convoluted tubule
options.C: Distal convoluted tubule
options.D: Collecting duct

explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule reabsorbs the largest share of filtered water, glucose, and essential ions back into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why is a rise in pressure inside the skull so harmful to the brain?

options.A: It immediately destroys the myelin sheath surrounding peripheral nerves
options.B: It triggers an excessive production of cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles
options.C: It causes the skull bones to expand and fracture outward
options.D: It squeezes blood vessels and reduces the flow of oxygen to brain cells

explanation: Makes total sense, right? The skull can't stretch, so high pressure squeezes the tiny blood vessels shut, cutting off vital oxygen to brain cells. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h4)

question: What does sustainability mean for a community health program?

options.A: The community can maintain the program after external funding ends
options.B: The program receives unlimited money from the government forever
options.C: Foreign experts run the project without stopping
options.D: No evaluation is ever required after setup

explanation: A sustainable program is built to last using local capacity and resources so it does not collapse when outside donors depart. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)

question: Which of these best describes probability sampling?

options.A: Participants are chosen simply because they are easy to find and talk to
options.B: The researcher hand-picks participants who agree with their hypothesis
options.C: Every member of the population has a known chance of being selected
options.D: Only patients with severe symptoms are allowed to join the study

explanation: Awesome! Probability sampling uses fairness and randomization, meaning nobody is unfairly favored and everyone has an equal shot at being picked. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is a frequent cause of a false-positive Mantoux test in individuals from other countries?

options.A: Prior vaccination with the BCG vaccine
options.B: Having a severe viral cold during testing
options.C: Receiving the injection too deep in the skin
options.D: Taking daily multi-vitamin supplements

explanation: The BCG vaccine, given in many countries to prevent childhood TB, can cause the immune system to react to PPD, creating a false-positive skin test. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h7)

question: Why do nurses use standard screening tools like the Patient Health Questionnaire in clinical practice?

options.A: To quantify and measure depression symptom severity
options.B: To measure blood levels of neurotransmitters
options.C: To test physical strength and muscular endurance
options.D: To diagnose specific neurological brain disorders

explanation: Exactly! Screening tools give us a clear, structured way to score how severe a patient's depressive symptoms are so we can track their progress. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T2#GNS324_U4_T2_h4)

question: When doing a quick physical check, which sign helps you spot possible anaemia?

options.A: Swelling of the lower legs
options.B: Pallor of the conjunctiva
options.C: Yellowing of the sclera
options.D: Redness of the palms

explanation: Easy and quick! Pulling down the lower eyelid lets you check the conjunctiva. If it looks pale instead of nice and pink, it's a quick clinical clue that the blood count might be low. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T020#GNS226_U2_T020_h4)

question: A nurse arrives in a new village to start a malaria project. What should she do FIRST?

options.A: Order the demolition of stagnant water pools near the houses
options.B: Distribute mosquito nets to the first people she meets on the road
options.C: Set up a treatment table in the market square and wait for patients
options.D: Visit the village chief and key community leaders to introduce herself

explanation: Proper community entry requires meeting leadership and building rapport before taking any health action. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h3)

question: A patient living near farm animals comes in with a suspected zoonotic infection. What is the best health advice to give them?

options.A: Tell them never to take medications for animal scratches
options.B: Suggest getting rid of every single animal in the neighborhood
options.C: Teach them safe food handling and how to protect themselves around animals
options.D: Tell them humans only catch things from other humans

explanation: Good hygiene, safe food prep, and protective gear go a long way in keeping animal germs away from humans. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h4)

question: How is locked-in syndrome different from true unconsciousness?

options.A: The patient experiences brief episodes of total memory loss
options.B: The patient responds only to painful physical pressure
options.C: The patient is fully aware but unable to move or speak
options.D: The patient sleeps for most of the day and night

explanation: Great job! In locked-in syndrome, their mind is completely awake and aware inside, they just can't move their muscles or talk. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a routine screening objective for inherited blood conditions in the community?

options.A: Providing immediate blood transfusions to healthy carriers
options.B: Raising public awareness about genetic counseling
options.C: Identifying carrier status before family planning
options.D: Detecting early signs of trait markers in newborns

explanation: Carriers of genetic blood traits are generally healthy and do not require blood transfusions. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h4)

question: A pregnant woman comes in for her first booking visit at 10 weeks. What is the main purpose of this early visit?

options.A: To administer high-dose oxytocin
options.B: To prepare the mother for immediate labor
options.C: To measure the baby's exact birth weight
options.D: To establish a baseline health assessment

explanation: This first visit lets us record vital signs, medical history, and early lab findings so we know her normal state of health. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h2)

question: Why do a pregnant woman's overall nutrient needs go up so much?

options.A: To make up for a complete shutdown of maternal digestion
options.B: To replace the need for normal maternal fat storage
options.C: To prevent the mother from ever experiencing physical fatigue
options.D: To support fetal growth, placental development, and maternal changes

explanation: You nailed it! Growing a baby and expanding your blood volume takes a lot of extra energy and building blocks from the foods mom eats. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T011#GNS227_U2_T011_h5)

question: What does the integrase enzyme do in the HIV life cycle?

options.A: It destroys circulating antibodies produced by B cells.
options.B: It manufactures new outer coats for budding virus particles.
options.C: It breaks down the outer cell wall of the host lymphocyte.
options.D: It inserts viral DNA into the host cell's genetic material.

explanation: Integrase acts like molecular glue, pasting the copied viral DNA right into the human host cell's DNA. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T1#GNS216_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is the most important first step when doing a sensitive reproductive health assessment?

options.A: Focusing solely on laboratory test results rather than patient words
options.B: Involving family members in every part of the interview process
options.C: Establishing a trusting and professional rapport to reduce anxiety
options.D: Immediately beginning the physical examination without asking questions

explanation: Spot on! Because talking about reproductive health can feel awkward or scary for patients, building trust first makes them feel safe enough to share the truth. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h6)

question: What main process causes osmotic diarrhoea?

options.A: Rapid muscle contractions moving food too fast to digest
options.B: Unabsorbed particles staying in the gut and drawing water in
options.C: Bacterial toxins directly forcing salt and water secretion
options.D: Bleeding ulcers leaking protein and blood into the bowel

explanation: Osmotic means pulling water! When certain substances aren't absorbed in your gut, they act like a magnet, drawing water right along with them into your stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why is community participation critical after a health plan has been created?

options.A: It prevents the local government from taxing the primary health center
options.B: It creates a sense of ownership so the community maintains the project
options.C: It ensures that health workers receive extra allowances from donors
options.D: It allows nurses to transfer all their daily workload to local volunteers

explanation: When communities participate in identifying and planning solutions, they protect and sustain the project long after external funding ends. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h6)

question: In clinical nursing, what is a 'toxidrome'?

options.A: An antidote given to reverse the effects of a specific snake venom
options.B: A group of signs and symptoms pointing to a specific class of poison
options.C: The physical damage caused by corrosive chemicals on the skin
options.D: The laboratory test used to measure blood alcohol concentration

explanation: Think of a toxidrome as a symptom 'syndrome' caused by a 'toxic' substance. It helps nurses quickly spot what kind of poison is at play! [learn more](GNS215_U5_T1#GNS215_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which of these practices is NOT safe for an HIV patient?

options.A: Drinking unboiled surface water during travel
options.B: Cooking all meats thoroughly
options.C: Washing raw fruits and veggies with clean water
options.D: Washing hands thoroughly before cooking

explanation: You got it! Unboiled water is packed with germs that cause severe diarrhea, which can quickly worsen malnutrition. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T5#GNS216_U6_T5_h7)

question: What is the medical name for the human breast glands?

options.A: Mammary glands
options.B: Salivary glands
options.C: Sweat glands
options.D: Sebaceous glands

explanation: Mammary glands are specialized modified sweat glands that produce milk in humans. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h1)

question: What is special about the mechanoreceptors sitting right near the surface of the skin?

options.A: They lack nerve fiber connections
options.B: They have small receptive fields for fine detail
options.C: They respond exclusively to extreme temperatures
options.D: They only detect deep, heavy pressure

explanation: Spot on! Because their receptive fields are small, superficial receptors help your brain pinpoint exact touches and feel fine textures. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T11#GNS211_U4_T11_h2)

question: Which breathing sign is a classic warning of active pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: A persistent cough lasting longer than three weeks
options.B: Sudden wheezing and severe shortness of breath
options.C: A sharp, barking cough triggered by cold air
options.D: Copious amounts of clear, watery nasal discharge

explanation: Any cough hanging around for more than three weeks should immediately make you think of TB and prompt a check-up! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h3)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to know how different hospital bed accessories work?

options.A: To calculate daily hospital room billing charges
options.B: To train housekeeping staff on proper linen folding
options.C: To select the right tool for a specific patient condition
options.D: To perform routine maintenance on mechanical bed frames

explanation: Brilliant! Knowing how each accessory works allows you to match the correct device to your patient's unique needs and prevent complications. Keep going! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is cold therapy (ice) applied during the first 24 to 48 hours following an acute soft tissue injury?

options.A: It increases blood flow to warm up the injured muscle
options.B: It causes vasoconstriction to reduce local swelling and pain
options.C: It forces white blood cells to leave the body entirely
options.D: It stimulates scar tissue to form much faster

explanation: Cold constricts local blood vessels, decreasing the amount of fluid that leaks into the surrounding injured tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h7)

question: How should a nurse handle it when a patient's cultural beliefs tell them to avoid certain healthy foods?

options.A: Ignore the dietary restriction and force the hospital meal anyway
options.B: Discontinue all nutritional counseling immediately
options.C: Scold the patient for holding unscientific traditional viewpoints
options.D: Provide respectful education and suggest culturally acceptable alternatives

explanation: Great nursing care means respecting our patients' backgrounds while gently helping them find safe, local food swaps that work for them. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h6)

question: A nurse wants to improve contraceptive acceptance in a traditional village. Which strategy is best?

options.A: Insulting the village traditions during public gatherings
options.B: Writing all health instructions in Latin
options.C: Banning husbands from attending health education talks
options.D: Engaging local community and religious leaders as health allies

explanation: Brilliant! Partnering with respected community figures builds immediate trust and helps lower resistance to reproductive health programs. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T006#GNS226_U6_T006_h8)

question: What is the most common bacteria that causes pneumonia outside of the hospital?

options.A: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.B: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.C: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.D: Influenza virus type A

explanation: Also known simply as pneumococcus, this bug is the leading culprit behind everyday community-acquired pneumonia. Great to keep in mind for clinicals! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why do international agreements like the Cairo Programme of Action matter for local Nigerian nursing practice?

options.A: They allow nurses to bypass local hospital rules during emergency obstetric procedures
options.B: They eliminate the need for patient consent in family planning clinics
options.C: They legally require international organizations to fund all local nursing salaries
options.D: They provide a standard framework that governments use to shape national health policies and clinic guidelines

explanation: Big global agreements help shape our national laws and clinic guidelines, which directly guide the safe and effective care you will provide to your patients. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical source of infection linked to Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: A recent streptococcal throat infection
options.B: An infected skin sore or boil
options.C: An untreated impetigo skin lesion
options.D: An inherited defect in heart valves

explanation: Heart valve issues are structural and something a person is born with, whereas glomerulonephritis is triggered by bacterial infections like throat sores or impetigo. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h3)

question: What role do descriptive studies play in nursing science?

options.A: They supply baseline facts that point toward areas needing clinical investigation
options.B: They replace clinical trials by proving which drugs cure diseases
options.C: They force patients to alter their daily health habits for better outcomes
options.D: They eliminate all errors found in previous medical journals

explanation: Descriptive studies act like our radar—they highlight where health issues lie, guiding nurses on what needs closer study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h2)

question: A young woman who had FGM as a child comes to your clinic with painful periods and trouble passing urine. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: A newly developed hormonal imbalance
options.B: An acute bacterial kidney infection
options.C: Scar tissue buildup and urethral obstruction
options.D: Normal physiological changes of aging

explanation: Years of healing leave tough scar tissue that can block the urinary and vaginal openings, making both urination and menstruation very painful. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h4)

question: What is the main difference between skin traction and skeletal traction?

options.A: Skin traction requires surgical pins placed in the bone
options.B: Skeletal traction uses much lighter weights than skin traction
options.C: Skin traction uses external devices attached to the skin
options.D: Skeletal traction is only used on the upper extremities

explanation: Skin traction applies pulling force from the outside using tapes, boots, or straps, while skeletal traction uses pins or wires placed directly into the bone. You've got this! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T8#GNS221_U1_T8_h1)

question: What happens legally to a nurse who performs FGM in countries with strict anti-FGM laws?

options.A: They must pay a small fine for using hospital supplies
options.B: They are reassigned to administrative duties without penalty
options.C: They can face imprisonment and lose their nursing license
options.D: They receive a simple warning from the local health board

explanation: Laws target medical practitioners directly, imposing heavy legal penalties and revoking their right to practice. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why do healthcare workers perform an Allen test before drawing an arterial blood gas (ABG) sample?

options.A: To verify adequate collateral circulation to the hand
options.B: To numb the puncture site before inserting the needle
